newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Vale to be controlled by holding - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Vale to be controlled by holding - paper.

text.p: Brazil will reveal Monday, when it releases the sale terms for Vale do Rio Doce, the creation of a Special Purpose Company to run state mining giant for five years after its privatization, a local newspaper said.

Gazeta Mercantil said the holding will be backed by a "golden shares" to be retained by the state after it sells off in February a strategic block of 45 percent of Vale's common voting shares in an initial privatization auction.
The government plans to sell off a total of 76 percent of common and 6.3 percent of preferred shares, which represent a 51-percent controlling stake in Vale, the paper said.
It said the 15-page document containing the sales terms confirms most of the privatization model approved last month by the National Privatization Council.
The document confirms the existance of two "golden shares," one for the Special Purpose Company and the other for Vale, it said.

The government's "golden share" will give it veto power to prevent the breaking of Vale's "synergistic links" and the new controllers of Vale will not be allowed to sell off a mine, railroad or port individually, it added.
